meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to turn out well, to succeed, to manage (impersonal + dative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'даться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to succeed, to manage', paired with 'удаваться'.

examples.text: Я не поняла, как тебе это удалось.
examples.trans: I didn't understand how you managed that.
And did you manage to find a room?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: How something is done. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
As an answer. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
+ accusative: через неделю = in a week
Core Russian prep meaning 'in (time); through' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Ordinal numeral. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fourth').

examples.trans: We live on the fourth floor.

examples.text: Вы когда взяли книгу Носова? В восемьдесят четвёртом году!
examples.trans: When did you borrow Nosov's book? In the year eighty-four!
